issues.name: Content without JavaScript
issues.details: Only 7 chars of server-rendered text — agents that never run JavaScript see an empty page.
issues.recommendation: Server-side render your homepage so AI crawlers see meaningful content without JavaScript. Ensure an H1 and 500+ chars of text in raw HTML.

issues.name: Agent crawler reachability
issues.details: AI crawlers hard-blocked: gptbot→403, claudebot→403, perplexitybot→403.
issues.recommendation: Allowlist the major AI crawler/agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, ora-agent, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF, bot-detection rules, and robots.txt so agents can reach your homepage.

issues.name: Not blocked by bot detection
issues.details: Bot-detection challenge served to automated agents (HTTP 403).
issues.recommendation: Allowlist known AI crawler user-agents at the edge.

issues.name: Agent-friendly 404s
issues.details: Fake path returned HTTP 401 instead of 404.
issues.recommendation: Return a real HTTP 404 (or 410) status for nonexistent paths - never a 200 with your app shell, which makes agents believe every path exists. For full credit, give the 404 response a short markdown body pointing agents at your sitemap, llms.txt, or docs index. Verify with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://yourdomain.com/some-path-that-does-not-exist` - it must print 404.

issues.name: OpenAPI spec published
issues.details: No OpenAPI specification found at conventional paths.
issues.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI 3.x spec and link it from your docs.

issues.name: Scoped permissions
issues.details: No securitySchemes/scopes in the API surface.
issues.recommendation: Define scoped permissions (read:/write:) so agents can request least privilege.

issues.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)
issues.details: Accept: text/markdown returned text/html; charset=utf-8; Vary: rsc, next-router-state-tree, next-router-prefetch, next-router-segment-prefetch.
issues.recommendation: Serve text/markdown when requested and set Vary: Accept on HTML responses.

issues.name: OAuth 2.0 support
issues.details: No OAuth support detected.
issues.recommendation: Implement OAuth 2.0 for API authentication. Publish your authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

issues.name: MCP server / manifest
issues.details: MCP discovery path serves an HTML page instead of a valid JSON manifest — agents cannot discover tools.
issues.recommendation: Build an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing your API as tools. Use Streamable HTTP transport for full score. This lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI agents call your product natively.

issues.name: Metadata completeness
issues.details: Only 1 of 6 metadata signals present in server HTML.
issues.recommendation: Add all four signals to your homepage: <link rel="canonical">, <html lang="...">, <meta property="og:image">, and <meta property="og:type">. Agents use these for entity resolution and attribution.

issues.name: JSON-LD structured data
issues.details: No JSON-LD structured data found on the homepage.
issues.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

issues.name: Organization schema completeness
issues.details: No Organization schema node found.
issues.recommendation: Add Organization JSON-LD that includes both contactPoint (with email/phone and contactType) and address (PostalAddress). This lets AI verify your business legitimacy and answer contact queries.

issues.name: Trust anchor pages
issues.details: Only 0 of 3 trust-anchor pages carry substantive content.
issues.recommendation: Publish real /about, /contact, and /privacy pages with at least 500 characters of content each. These are the pages AI agents check to verify your business is legitimate before recommending you.

issues.name: Sitemap exists
issues.details: No valid sitemap.xml found.
issues.recommendation: Publish a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml.

issues.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
issues.details: Instruction file at /.well-known/agents.md found but no when-to-use guidance.
issues.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.

issues.name: Rate limit response headers
issues.details: No live rate-limit headers on API responses.
issues.recommendation: Return RateLimit-* headers so agents can pace requests.

issues.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
issues.details: No public API documentation pages found.
issues.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.

issues.name: Developer portal
issues.details: No developer portal detected.
issues.recommendation: Create a developer portal at /developers with API keys, documentation, quickstart guides, and a sandbox environment.

issues.name: Public API with reachable endpoints
issues.details: No public API surface detected.
issues.recommendation: Expose a public REST or GraphQL API. AI agents need programmatic access  - not just a web UI  - to integrate with your product.

issues.name: API schema complexity analysis
issues.details: No OpenAPI spec found - nothing to analyse for reusable schemas.
issues.recommendation: Make your API spec self-describing: a unique operationId and a description on every operation, typed parameters, and response schemas. For GraphQL, a fully typed schema with a documented cost or rate limit reads best.

issues.name: Function calling compatibility
issues.details: No OpenAPI spec found - operations cannot be evaluated for LLM tool use.
issues.recommendation: Ensure API endpoints have unique operation IDs, typed schemas, and descriptions compatible with LLM function-calling formats.
